thread.title: As Markets Rally, Nothing's Changed But Our Perception

author: Barron's
title: As Markets Rally, Nothing's Changed But Our Perception
text:
Stocks look set for a higher open this morning following yesterday's rout as investors buy the dip.
Getty Images The S&P 500 has gained 1.1% to 2610.38 at 9:35 a.m. today, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average has risen 254.76 points, or 1.1%, to 24,115.22. The Nasdaq Composite has climbed 1.3% to 6864.02.
Of course, today's no different than yesterday--except when it comes to market prices. The economic outlook hasn't changed. The earnings outlook hasn't changed. All the fundamentals still look solid. But markets are forward looking, even if they sometimes react instantaneously to risks that should have been obvious. The bigger risk, though, is that the selloff does begin to impact the fundamentals.
"The US equity market is seemingly waking up to the idea that we are in a higher rate environment amid rising inflation and steady Fed hikes," writes Merrill Lynch economist Ethan Harris. "The equity market sell-off thus far does not alter our outlook for the US economy or monetary policy. However, if it turns into a sustained and broad-based deterioration of financial conditions, it would be a cause of concern."
That's a big if.
American International Group ( AIG ) has gained 2.1% to $59.51 despite reporting an adjusted profit of 52 cents a share, missing forecasts for 75 cents . "Despite the miss, we expect the shares to trade up on Friday on North American P&C progress that provides a template for fixing surprisingly weak International Commercial P&C results," writes KBW analyst Meyer Shields.
Expedia ( EXPE ) has tumbled 16% to $103.59 after reporting a fourth-quarter profit of 84 cents a share, missing forecasts for $1.15 as costs skyrocketed. "While we believe there may be greater competitive headwinds for Expedia than we anticipated, particularly on the vacation rentals side, we balance this view with the fact that Expedia remains the leading diversified travel platform in a $1.6 trillion travel market," writes Wells Fargo analyst Peter Stabler. "Therefore, while we are disappointed with the result, we think much of the broader longer term opportunity remains intact."
Getty Images Cboe Global Markets ( CBOE ) has fallen 3.1% to $107.75 after reporting an adjusted profit of 86 cents a share , below forecasts for 88 cents. Sales also missed estimates.
FireEye ( FEYE ) has soared 13% to $16.01 after reporting a fourth-quarter profit of 1 cent a share, better than the 2 cent loss predicted by analysts . Sales also beat the Street consensus. "FEYE met two important promises in the quarter; returning to growth and generating an operating profit," writes Evercore ISI analyst Ken Talanian.
Lions Gate Entertainment (LGF.A) have slumped 69% to $28.45 despite reporting a better-than-expected third-quarter profit and resuming its dividend payments. "On the call, management unexpectedly reset its three year OIBDA growth guide to mid-high single digits from low-mid teens, citing changes in the film release schedule in FY19," writes Piper analyst Stan Meyers.
Manitowoc ( MTW ) has jumped 8.7% to $37.38 despite reporting a 15 cent adjusted loss , worse than the 5-cent loss predicted by analysts, as sales of $481.5 million topped the Street consensus for $422.8 million. "We expect MTW shares to react favorably to 4Q earnings print as a result of the outsize orders and backlog growth," writes SunTrust analyst Charles Brady.
Nvidia (NVDA) has after climbed 10% to $239.20 after reporting a profit of $1.72 share , beating forecasts for $1.16, on sales of $2.9 billion, ahead of expectations for $2.7 billion.
Sarepta Therapeutics (SRPT) has dropped 6.4% to $53.50 after a drug trial was halted .
Skechers USA (SKX) has gained 4.8% to $40 after reporting an adjusted profit of 21 cents a sahre, beating forecasts for $13 cents a share.
United Parcel Service (UPS) has dropped 4.2% to $104.68 and FedEx (FDX) has fallen 4.1% to $229.50 after Amazon.com (AMZN) announced that it would launch a delivery service for businesses . Amazon has gained 1.3% to $1,368.
BorgWarner (BWA) has climbed 6.7% to $55.42 after getting upgraded to Outperform from Sector Perform at RBC.
Diamond Offshore Drilling (DO) has declined 1.5% to $14.70 after getting cut to Underperform from Market Perform at Raymond James.
iRobot (IRBT) has risen 2.8% to $61.46 after getting raised to Neutral from Underweight at JPMorgan.
Wynn Resorts (WYNN) has slipped 1.4% to $166.98 after getting cut to Equal Weight from Overweight at Morgan Stanley.
When the new tax law was passed, it led to a wave of speculation the private equity firms like KKR & Co . (KKR) and Apollo Global Management (APO) would convert from publicly traded partnerships into C-corp. And now Credit Suisse argues that there's a good chance it could happen soon for KKR.
In a note yesterday, Credit Suisse reiterated its Outperform rating on KKR, stating that it thinks there's about a 50% chance of the company converting its business from a publicly-traded partnership structure to a C-Corp by May. Such a change would potentially open the company's shares to additional investors who wouldn't be required to file K-1 tax forms.
Credit Suisse estimates that the shift to C-corp status could lead to a 30% to 50% expansion in the stock's multiple. "Additionally, while KKR is coming off a record fundraising year in 2017, there is a clear line of sight for another year of strong fundraising in 2018," Credit Suisse says.
Recently, Morgan Stanley wrote that shares of rival private equity firm Apollo could have a 26% upside if the company converted to C-Corp status. The company is currently analyzing the pros and cons of such a move. - John Kimelman
The irony was not lost on longtime Silicon Valley watchers.
On a day when the market crumbled and fabled FAANG stocks took a drubbing, a second-tier social media company, Twitter ( TWTR ) had a sparkling performance on Wall Street . Its shares surged as much as 22% before closing up 12% to $30.18, their highest closing price since Oct. 28, 2015. The stock is up 26% this year.
Reporting one's first profitable quarter on surprisingly strong advertising sales has that kind of effect on a company's stock when the DJIA is crumbling 4%.
Twitter Inc. GBH Insights analyst Daniel Ives deemed Twitter's first-ever profitable quarter a "blowout" with revenue ($731.6 million) that "crushed" street estimates. He called ad revenue "the star of the show" for Twitter's fourth quarter.
"The worst is over, the best is yet to come," trumpeted Global Equities Research, which established a price target of $34.
Tech's Fab Five - Facebook (FB), Apple (AAPL), Amazon (AMZN), Netflix (NFLX) and Alphabet (GOOGL) - didn't fare as well. They all declined at least 2.75%. On Monday, they collectively lost more than $90 billion in market value, according to CNBC .
Twitter left them all in the dust on Thursday. It traded as high as $35, its highest intraday level since July 28, 2015, when it peaked at $36.67. Jack Dorsey's other company is far from home free.
In a skeptical note, Monness, Crespi, Hardt doesn't foresee a sustainable recovery "since the fundamentals of the story and associated incentives to prospective users are virtually unchanged."
It has questions about the company's top ranks, with the recent departure of Chief Operating Officer Anthony Noto for online lender SoFi and additional pressures on Dorsey, who is Chief Executive Officer of Twitter and Square (SQ).
"It's not every day we see this much enthusiasm for a tech company becoming a high flyer by managing not to shrink, but here we are," concluded Monness, Crespi, Hardt, which remains Neutral on Twitter's stock.
Numbers don't lie. FAANG revenue and earnings dwarf Twitter's. And the micro-blogging company's user growth remain middling. Twitter's monthly active users grew 4% to 330 million year-over-year, below analyst expectations of 333 million. Facebook has 2.13 billion members. Yet those are concerns for another quarter.
For one day, at least, Twitter was king. - Jon Swartz
